The vibration damping device includes a tubular outer attachment member and an inner attachment member disposed relative to the outer attachment member. The two attachment members are coupled by first and second main rubber portions arranged at spaced-apart positions along the central axis of the device.

A partition portion is provided between the two main rubber portions and axially divides a liquid chamber into first and second liquid chambers. The partition portion includes an annular rigid portion defining a restricted passage through which the first and second liquid chambers communicate with each other.

The partition portion further includes an annular elastic portion positioned radially adjacent to the annular rigid portion. The elastic portion contacts the rigid portion without being bonded to it and is held in a radially compressed and deformed state.
outputs.L4:
A vibration damping device includes first and second mounting members connected by axially spaced main rubber portions. The mounting members and the main rubber portions define a sealed liquid chamber filled with a substantially incompressible liquid. A partition disposed between the main rubber portions divides the liquid chamber into two separate chambers. These chambers communicate with each other through a restricted passage, such as an orifice passage, so that vibration-induced deformation of the main rubber portions causes liquid to flow between the chambers.

The partition includes a rigid annular portion and an elastic annular portion formed from a rubber-like material. The elastic annular portion is fitted against the rigid annular portion in a radially compressed state. As a result, the elastic portion remains in close contact with the rigid portion through its restoring force, even though the two portions are not adhesively bonded or otherwise integrally joined at their interface. This arrangement provides a reliable seal and maintains the intended separation between the liquid chambers.

When vibration is applied to the device, the relative displacement of the mounting members changes the volumes and pressures of the two liquid chambers. The resulting pressure difference forces liquid through the restricted passage. Flow resistance, liquid resonance, and pressure variations within the chambers produce an effective damping action over a selected vibration-frequency range.

Because the elastic annular portion contacts the rigid annular portion without bonding, the partition can be manufactured and assembled more easily. The configuration reduces the need for adhesive treatment, vulcanization bonding, or other complicated interface-forming processes while retaining sufficient sealing performance and structural stability. The device therefore achieves effective liquid-mediated vibration isolation and damping with a simpler partition structure and improved manufacturing efficiency.

### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a particular person, place, object, or idea. Saying “a book” could mean any book, while “the book” points to a specific one.

Despite its simplicity, “the” gives language clarity and precision. It helps readers and listeners understand what is already known, unique, or especially relevant. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our everyday experience, and “the answer” when a particular answer is expected.

The word is so common that it often goes unnoticed. Nevertheless, without it, many sentences would sound unclear or unnatural. “The” demonstrates how even the smallest elements of language can carry great meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a liquid-filled vibration damping device with inner and outer attachment members, two axially spaced rubber portions, divided liquid chambers, a restricted passage, and an unbonded radially compressed elastic partition portion.
counterfactuals.output: A liquid-filled vibration damping device includes an inner attachment member, an outer attachment member disposed radially outward of the inner attachment member, and first and second rubber portions connecting the attachment members at axially spaced positions. A liquid-filled region defined between the attachment members and the rubber portions is divided by an elastic partition member into first and second liquid chambers. The liquid chambers communicate through a restricted passage configured to generate vibration-damping action based on liquid flow between the chambers. The elastic partition member includes a partition portion disposed between opposing support surfaces of the inner and outer attachment members. The partition portion is unbonded to at least one of the support surfaces and is radially compressed between the support surfaces, thereby being retained while permitting elastic deformation in response to pressure fluctuations in the liquid chambers. The arrangement facilitates assembly and provides controlled partition compliance while maintaining separation between the liquid chambers.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the construction of a vibration damping device using numbered reference signs, including the outer tube, inner attachment member, main rubber portions, partition, liquid chambers, rigid annular portion, elastic annular portion, and restricted passage.
counterfactuals.output:
A vibration damping device **(10)** is constructed as follows:

1. An **outer tube (12)** forms the cylindrical exterior of the device.  
2. An **inner attachment member (14)** is arranged generally coaxially inside the outer tube **(12)** and is adapted to be connected to a vibrating component.  
3. A pair of **main rubber portions (16, 18)** elastically connect the inner attachment member **(14)** to the outer tube **(12)** at axially spaced positions.  
4. A **partition (20)** is disposed between the main rubber portions **(16, 18)** and divides the sealed interior into a first liquid chamber **(22)** and a second liquid chamber **(24)**, both filled with a non-compressible damping liquid.  
5. The partition **(20)** includes a **rigid annular portion (26)** supported relative to the outer tube **(12)** and an **elastic annular portion (28)** extending between the rigid annular portion **(26)** and the inner attachment member **(14)**. The elastic annular portion **(28)** permits relative displacement while maintaining liquid-tight separation between the chambers.  
6. A **restricted passage (30)** communicates the first and second liquid chambers **(22, 24)**. Relative vibration between the outer tube **(12)** and the inner attachment member **(14)** deforms the main rubber portions **(16, 18)**, causing liquid to flow through the restricted passage **(30)**. Flow resistance and liquid resonance in the restricted passage generate the desired vibration-damping effect.

The first liquid chamber may be arranged on one side of the partition portion and configured as a pressure-receiving chamber whose volume varies in response to deformation of the elastic body, while the second liquid chamber may be arranged on the opposite side and configured as an equilibrium chamber having a flexible wall.
